lines.english: "Thank you for your call. This is the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office PLC."
"I sincerely apologize, but company operations are currently under a temporary hiatus."
"If you have urgent business, please contact the European branch of Touma Youko Office. The number to them is…"
"Just how long is Miyoko's vacation, exactly…?"
The call might have only lasted for a few seconds, but just imagining the fee for international calls to Japan makes my head hurt.
This is the tenth time since I first called her, and I've been greeted by the answering machine the entire month.
…Not to say that wasn't obvious after the third call.
"I'd like to hear Cloture."
It's been a month since Mom managed to bring herself to ask for that song…
Day in and day out, I've been searching for any orchestra willing to play that piece with me.
In fact, it's probably because I'm the one doing the searching that I'm struggling to find anyone.
At first, I used the time between my lessons to check the phone book for all orchestras from A to Z. After the third orchestra I tried to negotiate with…
If anything, it's only tarnished the reputation of Touma Youko Office further, because my negotiation skills are next to none.
How can everyone else carry conversations so smoothly without even seeing the person on the other line? That's a concept completely foreign to me.
After that, I resorted to emails.
It took me three days to get the computer running. Getting an email address and functioning internet took another three.
After nearly ten days worth of effort, the resulting message was sent to every single orchestra in the phone book, whose email addresses I found on the web.
About the pay, about the scheduling, about the venue…
Apparently, the traditional Japanese custom of "we'll cross that bridge when we get there" doesn't work on westerners.
"Ah, um… Emma-san? Ehm, I'm… Kazusa."
After seeing me run around like a headless chicken for nearly half a month, the headquarters of our European branch just couldn't bear to watch any longer.
"Yeah, and about what I needed. Ah, yes, right… Did you find them?"
Unfortunately though… Emma Bergen was more akin to a mere assistant to my mom back in the day. She didn't have the discretion nor knowledge that Miyoko had.
That's why the negotiations are still struggling. Currently, the number of orchestras who've even come to the negotiating table are…
"I see… not a single one."
That was the number.
"Yes, yes… Thank you. Call me if anything new comes up."
"Hah…"
This was a bitter pill to swallow.
I've allowed myself to completely misunderstand my value as a pianist, all thanks to that concert in Japan.
The name of the promising pianist "Touma Kazusa" doesn't mean anything here. It hasn't caught on at all.
The label of "Touma Youko's daughter" doesn't get me anywhere either.
People in this part of the world don't care for marketing slogans like that when it comes to music. It's a complete meritocracy.
At my wits' absolute end, I finally decided to dirty my hands through my forbidden last resort.
It's the means I hated most of all.
"That's right, the chief editor at Ensemble… I'm sure I had his business card."
I could sign a contract with a Japanese orchestra through the Japanese branch, invite them to Vienna, and hold an all-Japanese concert…
"…! What am I even saying? That's Kaiousha, isn't it…?"
I felt so cornered that I found no other choice but to rely on something that would probably end in failure… No, it would definitely end in failure.
But whatever the means, I must play Cloture for my mom.
Because there's no telling if this might be…
"Huh…?"
Just as I was getting lost in my thoughts, a pop-up appeared on my computer screen reading "new mail."
Checking the address, I noticed it was from the very first orchestra I sent a request to, but never got any response from.
But any hope I had as I opened the mail was quickly gone when I read its contents.
The writing was polite, but you could immediately tell it was a refusal.
"Ah…"
Yes, and underneath the polite refusal…
There was a letter of introduction to a different orchestra.
"…The Franz Dupre Orchestra?"
"Yes."
"…Franz Dupre accepted your request?"
"Yes."
Just as I expected…
Mom froze in place the moment she heard the name of that orchestra.
"So what will you do?"
"I'll do it. That's what you want, right?"
"Yeah but, this is Franz we're talking about… You hate his guts."
Franz Dupre…
A French conductor working out of Paris.
He's in his mid 30s. Even amongst the fierce competition that is typical of France, his skills are well attested to.
Any orchestra he commands always fills every seat at their concerts, and he's booked solid until next year.
His status and fame is international. A man of his stature should have no time for some upstart asian pianist like Touma Kazusa.
"I said I'll do it, so I will… But I still insist on the "Don't ever touch me" clause at the top of the contract."
…And he was once my mom's illicit lover.
And he also happens to be a bastard who tried to make advances on me in the past.
The only potential setback in our contract is this one issue.
"Well, you probably don't have to worry about that. That man turns into a different person when he's performing."
"…I can trust you on this, right?"
"Yes, no doubt about it. Besides, he could never lay his hands on you this time. After all, the one who set this whole thing up is probably…"
"Probably what?"
"No, forget it. More importantly, when's the concert?"
"Um… September 28th."
"Two months left, huh…"
"That's the only time their schedule is open. Apparently they had a big spat with a sponsor from New York and they had to cancel."
The very fact that the Franz Dubre Orchestra could even find an opening within the year is a miracle in and of itself.
That's what Emma told me after three minutes of silence on the phone.
"Very well, I'll make sure to survive until then. Come hell or high water."
"…Yeah, you go ahead and do that. I'll show you the best concerto you've ever heard."
At any rate, there's only two months left.
I'll have to somehow master Cloture before then.
I'll make sure that my efforts will reach her.
I'll make it in time, no matter what…
"Thank you… old man. Sorry if I end up passing on before you do."
